column1: # Long flags declared `standalone` in this scope while declared `valued` in many others.
# WHY THIS EXISTS. A valued flag mismodelled as `standalone` does not merely mis-describe the
# tool: the value it should have consumed falls through as a POSITIONAL. Where the flag carries a
# path gate that gate never fires, which is how `webpack -c /tmp/evil.js` auto-approved. The gated
# subset is covered by `a_gated_flag_is_never_declared_value_less`; this worklist is the UNGATED
# remainder, where nothing else would ever surface the mistake.
# HOW THE CANDIDATES ARE PICKED. Purely from the corpus, no external data: a `--name` means roughly
# the same thing across tools, so "valued in >= 5 scopes, standalone in at most a sixth of that"
# is evidence the odd one out is wrong. SHORT flags are deliberately excluded — `-o` is an output
# path in one tool and a boolean in the next, so the same comparison there is noise, and they are
# the bulk of the raw overlap (`-r` alone overlaps in 34 scopes).
# IT IS A HEURISTIC, NOT A VERDICT. Some rows will be correct as written — a tool really can have a
# boolean `--filter` when everyone else's takes a value. Resolving a row means checking that ONE
# tool's grammar and then either moving the flag to `valued` / `optional_valued`, or deleting the
# row because the declaration was right.
# SHRINKS ONLY. `a_long_flag_is_not_standalone_where_it_is_valued_elsewhere` fails if a scope
# appears that is not listed here, so a new mismodelling cannot land quietly. It also fails on a
# row that is no longer a candidate, so fixing a command means deleting its row in the same change
# and the file cannot rot into a list of things that were true once.
# Seeded 2026-08-29 with 118 rows. Found and fixed while seeding it: pre-commit's `-c`/`--config`
# on install / uninstall / install-hooks / autoupdate (a config PATH, and `install` writes git
# hooks) and `-j`/`--jobs` on autoupdate (a thread count) — both confirmed against pre-commit.com.
